title: The Battle of Hastings
description: October 1066. William of Normandy's invasion army faces King Harold's Anglo-Saxon shield wall on Senlac Hill. The player commands the Norman force and must break the shield wall through feigned retreats and combined cavalry-archer assaults before nightfall ends the battle.

issues_found: GAIA roster places 2,400 oak trees on a 120x120 map, making Senlac an enclosed forest; the battlefield was an open ridge with the Andredsweald only at the Norman rear, and heavy woodland undercuts the cavalry-charge/feigned-retreat premise the text builds the mission on

Economic furniture inappropriate to a single-day pitched battle: Town Centers, 7 Houses, Barracks, Stable, Archery Range, Monastery, 10 gold mines, 8 stone mines, sheep and forage bushes for a battle that involved no settlement or production
Norman infantry is badly under-weighted (6 spearmen against 10 knights and 6 light cavalry); at Hastings the Norman line was mostly infantry with cavalry as the exploiting arm
No terrain elevation or marsh is evidenced in the placed content, so the defensive advantage of the hill named in the narration is asserted in text only
The 'Feigned Retreat' and 'Fyrd Lured' triggers only fire DISPLAY_INSTRUCTIONS; the decisive tactic of the battle is narrated rather than mechanically rewarded

Closing text 'William's claim to the English throne stands unopposed' overstates the outcome — Dover, London and the northern earls submitted only after further campaigning, and rebellions followed for years
